title: bug: a parked wait_for_task re-matches only on TASK_CREATED and TASK_UPDATED, so a delete_task that makes a legacy dependent claimable (its only unmet prerequisite is gone) never wakes the waiting seat
description:
Held item from hunt #11 (task-afe61cc0, architect-74d9e1c7, msg-7ed73235), filed by the governor in BACKLOG. It edits tools/waitForTask.ts, the same file as task-4fbd3c69 (wait_for_task vs the caller's finalizing attempt), so it waits on that row. The governor promotes it once 4fbd3c69 is DONE. Impact is low.

PROBLEM. For a legacy (non verified-local) consumer a missing prerequisite counts as satisfied, so deleting a dependent's only unmet prerequisite makes the dependent claimable. But delete emits TASK_DELETED, and a parked wait_for_task re-matches only on TASK_CREATED and TASK_UPDATED. The waiting seat sleeps until its timeout or an unrelated update.

EVIDENCE (at 8ca8d389):
- waitForTask.ts:435 `if (event.type !== 'TASK_CREATED' && event.type !== 'TASK_UPDATED') return;`
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-afe61cc0/A/zzHuntA_waitDeleteWake.test.ts with its .output.txt. "wakes a parked WORKING waiter when deleting its only unmet prerequisite makes the dependent claimable" fails, "Tests 1 failed (1)".

FIX DIRECTION. Also re-run the existing findMatchingTask match on TASK_DELETED, and on any other event that can change dependency readiness, such as TASK_ARCHIVED if it is not already covered. Keep the wake/cleanup path unchanged.
definitionOfDone: A wait_for_task parked for WORKING rows wakes with the dependent row when delete_task removes that row's only unmet prerequisite, and an unrelated TASK_DELETED still doesn't wake it.
The ported hunt repro passes, and the existing wait_for_task test files stay green in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
docs/MCP_SERVER.md, `### moe.wait_for_task` section only, with your Edit tool. Make three phrase edits and nothing else:
(a) About :1576, the Returns comment `// Task available (immediately, or on a TASK_CREATED/TASK_UPDATED wake):` becomes `// Task available (immediately, or on a TASK_CREATED/TASK_UPDATED/TASK_DELETED wake):`.
(b) About :1610, at the end of the **Dependency gating matches `claim_next_task`** note, after `so a parked dependent wakes the moment its last prerequisite lands.`, append one sentence: `The` + ` TASK_DELETED` (in backticks) + ` that` + ` moe.delete_task` (in backticks) + ` publishes re-runs it too, so a legacy or observe dependent whose last unmet prerequisite is deleted wakes at once (a deleted id counts as satisfied for it).`
(c) About :1613, `Wake triggers while parked: ` followed by the backticked `TASK_CREATED`/`TASK_UPDATED` and ` producing a claimable match;` becomes the backticked `TASK_CREATED`/`TASK_UPDATED`/`TASK_DELETED` followed by ` producing a claimable match (a delete that frees nothing leaves the wait parked);`.
No daemon test asserts these phrases; the doc tests under src/util check other text.

Then delete only the gate dirs you made, by fingerprint. A dir qualifies only if it is a /tmp/tmp.* dir, passes `[ -O "$d" ]`, and its packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/waitForTask.deleteWake.test.ts contains `task-b7203d89 (hunt #11)`. /tmp is shared with other seats, so never delete by name pattern alone, and never pattern-kill a process (rail).

Adversarial self-review of your `git diff` plus the new file. Fix any finding, re-run step 4, then call complete_task.
(1) Scope: waitForTask.ts changes only the filter line and its comment, and MCP_SERVER.md only the three phrases. The new test file is the only other change.
(2) Over-waking: a delete wakes only through findMatchingTask, the same predicate a create or update runs. (w1) and (w3) prove that a delete which frees nothing leaves the wait parked.
(3) NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP: suppose a delete frees a row that only the solo epic+status rule withholds. A team-less caller now wakes with that remedy, exactly as the matching create or update would wake it. That is intended.
(4) Pending questions: that branch still requires TASK_UPDATED, so a deleted row's hasPendingQuestion wakes nobody.
(5) Cost: delete_epic deletes its tasks one by one through deleteTask. Each delete emits TASK_DELETED and re-runs the matcher once per parked waiter, the same per-event cost every update already pays.
(6) Concurrency: the listener runs synchronously inside emit, after the row is gone. cleanup() unsubscribes before resolve, so two deletes in a row cannot resolve one wait twice.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A moe.wait_for_task parked for WORKING rows re-runs its claimable match on TASK_DELETED as well as on TASK_CREATED and TASK_UPDATED. When delete_task removes a legacy or observe dependent's last unmet prerequisite (a deleted dependsOn id counts as satisfied), the wait wakes with that dependent, and the claim that follows hands it out. A delete that frees nothing re-runs the match, finds none and leaves the wait parked.
acceptanceCriteria: (w1) Deleting task-other, which no row depends on, leaves worker-1's wait parked (still in activeWaiters).

(w2) Deleting task-prereq, task-dep's only unmet prerequisite, resolves the wait with hasNext true, task task-dep and nextAction moe.claim_next_task. A WORKING claim by worker-1 then hands out task-dep.
(w3) Deleting task-gate-a, one of task-dep2's two unmet prerequisites, leaves the wait parked. Deleting task-gate-b then wakes it with task-dep2.

At base 54635828 the new file reads 2 failed | 1 passed (3), with (w2) and (w3) failing. With the fix, tsc is clean and the waitForTask, deleteTask, dependencyUnblock and waiter-ownership suites pass: 6 files, 86 tests.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md's wait_for_task section names TASK_DELETED in three places: the Returns comment, the dependency-gating note and the wake-trigger list.
invariants: The pending-question branch still keys on TASK_UPDATED only, and the MESSAGE_CREATED branch is unchanged.
A delete wakes a waiter only through findMatchingTask: with a claimable match, or with the NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP remedy that a create or update would also give.
No new error handling path: a throw in the re-match is caught by StateManager.emit, as for created and updated events.
No new state, timer or subscription. The only change is a wider event filter in the existing listener.
compatibility: No schema or MCP contract change. The wake answers keep their shapes; one more event can now trigger them.
delete_epic deletes its tasks through deleteTask, which publishes TASK_DELETED for each, so an epic delete re-runs the match too.
A verified-local dependent is unaffected. The matcher already skips verified-local rows, and a missing prerequisite never satisfies one.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) Chosen: widen the parked listener's event filter to TASK_DELETED, so a delete re-runs the same findMatchingTask predicate a create or update runs. It is one line, and it inherits dependency gating, finalizing holds, profile admission and the team rule unchanged.
(2) Rejected: a delete-specific wake that looks up rows naming the deleted id in dependsOn. It wakes a dependent that still has another unmet prerequisite (that mutant fails (w3)), and it duplicates the claim predicate.
(3) Rejected: having delete_task publish a TASK_UPDATED per dependent. It broadcasts rows that did not change (phantom board updates), and the governor asked to keep the edit inside the filter.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Hunt repro: after delete_task removed the prerequisite, the parked wait timed out (hasNext false, timedOut), although an immediate claim would have handed out the dependent.
deleteEpic cascades through deleteTask, which emits TASK_DELETED per task, so epic deletes are covered too.

planningNotes.risks:
Sibling task-c8618ccd (WORKING) edits waitForTask.ts's pending-question path about 28 lines below this hunk, so the landing merge is clean. If it ever conflicts, keep both changes.
The tests use 50 ms ticks and a 3000 ms wait. With the fix the wake is synchronous on the delete, so the ticks only let the waiter register. Do not shorten the wait below 1000 ms, because the tool clamps it.
Error handling stays as it is: no new throw site.
